classification.difficultyReason: Apply the explicitly requested vertical line test to supplied curves, recognising that zero intersections are permitted and multiple intersections fail.

content.prompt: Use the vertical line test to determine whether each graph is the graph of a function.

spec.description: Horizontal line with its supplied y-axis point. Source origin O omitted under the graph convention.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the horizontal line $y=4$ exactly once, so the graph passes the vertical line test.

spec.description: Vertical line x=3 with supplied x-axis point; no test line added.

answer.worked: The vertical line $x=3$ coincides with the graph and meets it at more than one point. The graph fails the vertical line test.

spec.description: Upward parabola, marked vertex (0,3), equation label above the curve; axes have no invented ticks.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the parabola exactly once. The graph passes the vertical line test.

spec.description: Increasing cubic through the origin, without added point markers or numeric ticks.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the cubic exactly once. The graph passes the vertical line test.

spec.description: Circle with centre (2,3), radius 5, equal coordinate scales and both axis crossings retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied question graph and centre only.

answer.worked: The vertical line $x=2$ cuts the circle twice, at $(2,8)$ and $(2,-2)$. The graph fails the vertical line test.

spec.description: Two hyperbola branches, dashed x=3 asymptote, y-intercept label -5/3, and horizontal asymptote supplied by the x-axis.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph and asymptote only; no vertical test line.

answer.worked: Every vertical line with $x\ne3$ meets the graph once. The line $x=3$ meets it zero times. Thus every vertical line meets the graph at most once, so it passes the vertical line test.

spec.description: Logarithmic graph with dashed x=-5 asymptote and marked intercepts (-4,0) and (0,1).
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph, intercepts and asymptote only.

answer.worked: A vertical line with $x>-5$ meets the curve once; a vertical line with $x\le-5$ does not meet it. The graph passes the vertical line test.

spec.description: Horizontal ellipse with all four marked and labelled axis intercepts.

answer.worked: The vertical line $x=0$ cuts the ellipse at $(0,1)$ and $(0,-1)$. The graph fails the vertical line test.

spec.description: Left-opening parabola with its vertex marked at the origin and equation above the upper branch.

answer.worked: The vertical line $x=-1$ cuts the graph at $(-1,1)$ and $(-1,-1)$. The graph fails the vertical line test.
